title: Reasons for Wrong Charging of GST by Government Agencies and Review of Processes to Prevent Recurrence
what_it_is: Reasons for Wrong Charging of GST by Government Agencies and Review of Processes to Prevent Recurrence

sections.label: GST review of government fees
sections.summary: MOF and IRAS found inconsistencies in GST on certain Government fees, identifying 18 regulatory fees wrongly charged GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It was picked up by MOF and IRAS as part of our regular internal review of the GST regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We discovered inconsistencies in the application of GST on certain Government fees in November 2023 and concluded the review in January 2024, with 18 regulatory fees identified to have charged GST wrongly and need to be refunded.

sections.label: GST refunds with interest
sections.summary: Agencies stopped charging GST on the 18 fees and will refund affected taxpayers with 5.5% annual interest, covering transactions since 1 January 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As announced on 14 February, the agencies involved have ceased charging GST on the 18 fees and will refund all affected taxpayers with interest of 5.5% per annum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The refund will minimally cover transactions since 1 January 2019 as the agencies, as GST-registered entities, are required by law to keep records for five years.

sections.label: Bill to amend GST Act
sections.summary: MOF will table a Bill to amend the GST Act to clarify GST treatment for such fees and prescribe a list of regulatory fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: MOF will table a Bill soon to amend the GST Act to clarify the GST treatment for such fees, and to prescribe a list of regulatory fees where GST should not be charged.

sections.label: List of regulatory fees
sections.summary: A list of regulatory fees where GST should not be charged will be prescribed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As I explained in my main reply, we will prescribe a list of the regulatory fees where GST should not be charged.

sections.label: Review found 18 fees
sections.summary: By January the review was completed and 18 fees were identified as needing rectification, with wrongly collected GST refunded to taxpayers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: By January, we completed the review and we identified that there are 18 fees altogether that would need to be rectified and the GST that is wrongly collected, will have to be refunded to taxpayers.

sections.label: Refund with 5.5% interest
sections.summary: The Minister said the refund would be made together with interest at 5.5% per annum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Second, the Minister said that the refund would be made together with interest at 5.5% per annum.

sections.label: Interest rate for Government refunds
sections.summary: The 5.5% rate was set referencing the prevailing interest rate for Government refunds, the average prime lending rate compiled by MAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The second question about interest rates, the rate of 5.5% was set referencing the prevailing interest rate for Government refunds over the affected period and that is the average prime lending rate, compiled by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) from leading banks and licensed companies.
